rows.source: MCA Coastguard search and rescue collection
rows.verified: The official collection provides coastal, beach, sailing and search-and-rescue safety information.
In a coastal emergency, callers should dial 999 and ask for the Coastguard.
At sea, an emergency can be raised through a Mayday distress alert on VHF Channel 16 or by calling 999 for the Coastguard.
Administrative email addresses must not be used to pass operational search-and-rescue information.
At sea, Global Maritime Distress and Safety System equipment can be used to send distress or urgency alerts.
HM Coastguard regularly broadcasts Maritime Safety Information by radio.
Maritime Safety Information includes navigational guidance and warnings.
Mariners are required to check Maritime Safety Information together with weather and tide information to reduce collision and accident risk.

rows.source: Met Office beach and tide guide
rows.verified: The guide distinguishes incoming or flooding tides from receding or ebbing tides.

rows.source: Met Office beach and tide guide
rows.verified: An incoming tide can remove a safe route back around a beach or cove.

rows.source: Met Office beach and tide guide
rows.verified: Anyone cut off by the tide should call 999 and ask for the Coastguard.
People in trouble at the coast or in the sea should call 999 and ask for HM Coastguard.
The rescue-coordination-centre contact page was updated on 9 July 2026.

rows.source: MCA Coastguard search and rescue collection
rows.verified: Personal information gathered during emergency response is processed to coordinate rescue and preserve safety of life.

rows.source: MCA Coastguard search and rescue collection
rows.verified: Emergency information may be shared with relevant global search-and-rescue bodies, UK police and other 999 services, RNLI and MAIB where necessary.

rows.source: MCA Coastguard search and rescue collection
rows.verified: Emergency-response data processing is described as part of the MCA's public task.
Office contact details are for routine business; emergencies must use the Coastguard distress routes.

rows.source: Met Office beach and tide guide
rows.verified: Beach forecasts and tide times support planning before coastal visits and help avoid tidal cut-off.
Workers in tidal areas should plan to be safely ashore before any possibility of being cut off by the tide.
In tidal-area emergencies, official guidance directs users to 999 for HM Coastguard or Marine Band Radio Channel 16.

rows.source: MCA Coastguard search and rescue collection
rows.verified: HM Coastguard emergency coordination can involve police, other UK 999 services, RNLI and accident investigators.

rows.source: MCA Coastguard search and rescue collection
rows.verified: Coastal warnings, tide guidance and rescue routes are situational safety context and are not converted into static parcel-level risk scores.
